help.tips[0].examples[0].en: He brought the letter and thought nothing of it.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: We didn't know the way and were at a loss.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: denken is a mixed verb: the stem changes to dach- and takes -te, so ich dachte.
help.tips[0].en.text: bringen → brachte, denken → dachte, wissen → wusste, kennen → kannte, nennen → nannte, rennen → rannte, brennen → brannte, senden → sandte (or sendete), wenden → wandte (or wendete). Endings like any -te verb: brachte, brachtest, brachte, brachten, brachtet, brachten.
help.tips[0].en.title: New vowel + -te
help.tips[0].en.trap: 'er denkte', 'er wisste', 'er kennte' are the errors: the -te is right but the vowel must change too.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: I didn't know that. I knew him well.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: We thought of you and brought you something.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: The participle keeps the changed stem: ge- + brach + -t = gebracht.
help.tips[1].en.text: gebracht, gedacht, gewusst, gekannt, genannt, gerannt, gebrannt, gesandt, gewandt — ge- + changed stem + -t. The Präteritum and the participle share their vowel.
help.tips[1].en.title: The participle keeps the changed stem
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: As a child I didn't like spinach and wasn't allowed to stay up late.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: We had to wait because we could not come earlier.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: In the Präteritum the modal loses its umlaut and adds -te: dürfen → durfte.
help.tips[2].en.text: können → konnte, müssen → musste, dürfen → durfte, mögen → mochte: the umlaut disappears and -te is added. sollen → sollte and wollen → wollte have no umlaut to lose. haben → hatte belongs here too.
help.tips[2].en.title: The modals are mixed too
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: The fire was burning, and everyone ran outside.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: rennen works like kennen: e becomes a, the double n stays, and -te is added: rannte.
help.tips[3].en.text: kennen, nennen, rennen, brennen → kannte, nannte, rannte, brannte. Same shape, same change. Learn them as a chant.
help.tips[3].en.title: The four -ennen verbs
help.context.en: When the house was burning, my neighbour ran to us and brought the children to safety. Nobody knew how the fire had started. The fire brigade later named a faulty stove as the cause. I knew that stove – I had connected it myself, and I thought about it all night.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: The participle uses the changed stem.
help.mistakes[3].whyEn: For broadcasting only the regular form sendete is used.
help.hookEn: bringen, denken, wissen, kennen: nine everyday verbs change their vowel and add -te, so brachte, dachte and wusste come out right.
help.introEn: A small third group of verbs mixes the two systems: they change their vowel like a strong verb and take the -te of a weak verb. There are only nine of them, and they are among the commonest verbs in the language: bringen → brachte (gebracht), denken → dachte (gedacht), wissen → wusste (gewusst), kennen → kannte (gekannt), nennen → nannte (genannt), rennen → rannte (gerannt), brennen → brannte (gebrannt), senden → sandte (gesandt), wenden → wandte (gewandt). The last two also have regular forms — sendete, wendete — which are just as correct and are the only possible forms for a broadcast (Das Radio sendete …) or for turning a car (Er wendete das Auto). The modals follow the same pattern: können → konnte, müssen → musste, dürfen → durfte, mögen → mochte, and haben → hatte. Note the consonant change in bringen and denken (ng/nk → ch: brachte, dachte) and the vowel e → a in kennen, nennen, rennen, brennen. The participle keeps the same changed stem with ge- + -t.
help.rememberEn[0]: Vowel changes AND -te: brachte, dachte, wusste, kannte.
help.rememberEn[1]: bring/denk → brach-/dach-: ng and nk become ch.
